reasoning: Round 2 corrections from the supervisor: (1) the dividend is $2.49 now ($0.6232/qtr) growing 6% to $2.64 in 2027. My round-1 number was right but the derivation was wrong, and it is now fixed. (2) The Street-target leg was circular and is dropped. (3) NEE, not Dominion, pays a $4.83B (~$2.30/share) regulatory termination fee, so a rejection is costly. I put ~15% on a regulatory failure being priced by the horizon, about $0.35/share of expected cost; the offsetting removal of dilution makes me net it to ~$0.3 including Uri. (4) The Sep 29 Oklahoma Uri liability ruling is added as an unquantified tail. I could not find a dollar figure for what NEM billed Oklahoma buyers. New in-lane checks of dockets and local press: SC PSC docket 2026-186-EG sets ORS and intervenor testimony for Oct 28, rebuttal Nov 18, hearing Dec 8 and a final order ~Jan 29 2027. The concession gap is checkable: the $2.25B shareholder-funded credit package is unchanged in total, with Virginia's $1.78B share. Virginia's extension from 2 to 4 years came from reallocating data-center credits, plus ~$90M of new money. So SC+NC hold ~$0.47B, and SC parity would cost roughly a few hundred million dollars (~$0.1-0.2/share), not thesis-relevant. The governor declined a special session to extend the VA deadline (a modest positive for timing), but she and the AG both intervene and call current terms 'not sufficient', so more concessions are likely. The cost is small versus a ~$158B market cap. Valuation: P/E $81.3 (NTM $4.58 x 17.75x), dividend yield $80.0, blended $80.8, less $0.3 = $80.5 (was $83). Scenarios: 60/80/98 at 22/58/20, mean ~$79.2, median ~$79.5. Ladder: lognormal centered at $79.5 with 22% vol, a heavier left tail for deal and Uri risk, and a slightly thinner upper tail than round 1. P(>=76) is 0.575 (was 0.58), P(>=83) is 0.415 (was 0.43).
